name: Discord MCP
tagline: Send messages, read channels, manage servers from your AI agent.
shortDescription: The Discord MCP server. Lets your agent send messages to channels, read recent channel history, list servers and channels, manage roles, and post embeds. Uses Discord bot tokens for auth.
longDescription:
## What it is

A community-built Discord MCP server. Exposes the Discord API as MCP tools: send messages, read channel history, list servers/channels/users, manage roles, post rich embeds, and add reactions. Auth is a standard Discord bot token.

## Why we recommend it

If your community or team uses Discord, this is the cleanest way to give an agent the ability to post updates, summarize conversations, or answer questions in a channel. The auth model is the same Discord bot token you'd use for any other bot, so you can use existing roles and permissions to scope what the agent can do.

## When to use it

- Community managers: agent posts release notes, answers FAQs, summarizes threads
- DevOps alerts: agent posts build failures, deploy events, on-call escalations to a private channel
- Team coordination: agent reads recent messages in a channel and posts a daily standup summary
- Customer support: agent monitors a support channel and posts initial responses
installInstructions:
1. Create a Discord application at https://discord.com/developers/applications
2. Create a bot for the application, copy the bot token
3. Set `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=...`
4. Invite the bot to your server with appropriate permissions (Send Messages, Read Message History)
5. `npx -y discord-mcp`
pricingDetails: Free. The MCP server is open source. Discord is free for any number of users.
